messages:
Maya: ping, Support ticket from Merchant 'BlueCart' — they say requests pinned to us-east started getting 307s to eu-west and then auth failures. Full repro in ticket.
Customer-SRE: repro steps I ran with their token (sanitized):
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer tok_us_east_BLUECART_xxx\" \n  -H \"X-Region: us-east-1\" \n  -d '{\"input\":\"test\"}'
--- response headers ---
HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect
Location: https://eu-west-1.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
x-fallback-reason: pool_exhausted

Customer-SRE: when client follows Location they get 403 because token is region-scoped to us-east. Also observed 429s earlier.
Alex: is this Dedicated or Hosted for that tenant? any autoscaler alerts?
Maya: Dedicated pool (us-east-ded-3), they had sudden traffic burst around 2026-06-10T18:12Z. Manual burst policy enabled. Autoscaler hit max_instances at 18:14Z.
Jin: infra metrics show async_queue_depth peaked at 11800 at 18:15Z, worker_util ~99%. Router triggered spillover policy when queue_depth > overflow_threshold ( configured 5000 ). It selected eu-west-1 as fallback.
Priya: router logs show tag=spillover_autoroute and sticky_assign=300s. Once a session fell back to eu-west it remained sticky for TTL.
Alex: explains prolonged EU routing. Why 307 instead of proxying the request through router?
Jin: security rule: if token_scope != dest_region we return 307 with x-fallback-reason to avoid forwarding region-scoped tokens cross-region. Router emits Location header pointing to fallback endpoint.
Priya: consequence: many clients treat 307 as fatal or don't resend with proper credentials; result is a wave of 403/401s and significant p95 latency increase due to round-trip + retries.
Customer-SRE: timeline from customer logs: 18:10 first 429s, 18:13 queue climbing, 18:15 first redirects (307), then 403s when following redirect.
Maya: immediate mitigations we discussed:
- short-term: lower sticky_ttl for this pool (e.g., 60s) so sessions revert faster once load normalizes
- short-term: request emergency burst capacity (if tenant commit permits)
- medium-term: raise overflow_threshold for Dedicated tenants during business hours to prefer queueing over immediate fallback
- long-term: design cross-region token validation or short-lived relay tokens (security review required)
Jin: quick plan: request +2 nodes to the dedicated pool and change sticky_ttl=60 and overflow_threshold=9000 for peak hours. I can apply changes after approvals (~45-90m).
Priya: SDK improvement: detect 307 with x-fallback-reason and show explicit message: "region fallback: token invalid for fallback region; obtain multi-region token or retry after routing stabilizes". Also consider optional client-side automatic backoff + retry to original region when TTL expires. ETA 48h for publish.
Alex: infra action items: scale pool now, lower sticky_ttl, add metric emission for fallback_redirects and auth_mismatch_redirects so we can alert per-tenant when redirects >0.5%.
Jin: paste sanitized router log for the event:
[2026-06-10T18:15:23Z] router=route-9 pool=us-east-ded-3 tenant=bluecart action=redirect dst_region=eu-west-1 reason=pool_exhausted queue_depth=11804 sticky_ttl=300 emit_tag=spillover_autoroute
[2026-06-10T18:15:23Z] http_out status=307 location=https://eu-west-1.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate x-fallback-reason=pool_exhausted token_scope=us-east-1

Maya: filing internal incident INC-RED-2026-511 and linking customer ticket. Assigning Jin + Priya. Tagging @oncall for awareness.
SRE-bot: Incident INC-RED-2026-511 created by Maya. Priority: P2. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-RED-2026-511
Maya: I'll keep the customer updated. Please paste approval and console changes here once done. Customer asked for ETA on stable routing (prefer no cross-region redirects).
